newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up in nearbys on Brazil talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up in nearbys on Brazil talk.

text.p: CBOT soybeans closed mixed with nearby months higher on talk Brazil was seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans plus followthrough from Tuesday's firm close, traders said.
Commercial buying, centered in the January, magnified the gains and volume was light, allowing that demand to move prices higher.
Brazilian soybean traders were surprised at talk that Brazilian buyers would be buying U.S. soybeans but did not rule out the possibility.
Tight nearby stocks and slow farmer selling added support.
Gains were limited when January encountered chart resistance in the vicinity of $7.15 per bushel. The session high for January was $7.16-1/2.
Technicians said first resistance in the January was at $7.15-3/4 and second resistance at $7.23-1/2. First support was at $7.08 and second support at $7.00-1/4.
Trading was muted and the CBOT grains futures session closed at 1210 CST because of the U.S. Thanksgiving Day Holiday Thursday.
Soybeans closed 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 1-3/4 lower, with January up 2-1/4 at $7.15-1/4.
Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of January, Refco Inc bought 1.5 million January and sold three million January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 31,000 contracts, below the 39,296 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, ADM Investor Services sold 200 January $7.25 calls at 5-1/2 to 5-3/8 cents, Cargill Investor Services sold 300 January $7.25 puts at 16 cents and bought 300 January $7.25 calls at five cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, below the 8,718 traded Tuesday.
